key_insight: Tree-based machine learning models can accurately predict halide perovskite band gaps from simple atomic and structural descriptors, revealing that B-site and X-site chemistry dominate the trend.
engineering_relevance: The results offer a fast screening tool for designing low-toxicity perovskites with targeted band gaps, reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error synthesis and computation.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors on atomic and structural descriptors.
Compared RFR, GBRT, and XGB for band gap prediction across multiple halide perovskite families.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify the most influential composition variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy for RFR, GBRT, and XGB across a wide range of halide perovskite band gaps.
watch_item: Model transferability may be limited if new perovskite chemistries or structural motifs fall outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
